chunks: 1983 - Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"If a man travels during the month of Ramaḍān and departs after midday, he must fast that day, and it is counted for him as part of Ramaḍān. وإذا he enters a land before the rise of dawn while intending to reside there, then he must fast that day. But if he enters after the rise of dawn, then no fasting is obligatory upon him, though if he wishes he may fast."

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: residence or staying in a place with intention to remain
key_terms.بَعْدَ نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ: after midday, the point after which departure does not cancel that day's fast
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the obligatory month of fasting
key_terms.صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ: fasting that day as an obligatory observance
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rise of dawn, the start time relevant to fasting obligation
key_terms.فَلَا صِيَامَ عَلَيْهِ: no fasting is obligatory upon him in that case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting in Ramaḍān if a traveler leaves after midday or arrives before or after dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on fasting during travel in the month of Ramaḍān. It distinguishes between departing after midday and arriving before or after dawn, clarifying when the fast of that day remains binding and when it is not obligatory.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1983 - Al-‘Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Imam Abu Abdullah (as):

"If a man travels during the Month of Ramadan and departs after midday, he must fast that day, and it will be counted as part of his Month of Ramadan fast. However, if he enters a place before dawn with the intention of staying there, he is obligated to fast that day. But if he enters after dawn, fasting is not obligatory for him, although he may fast if he wishes."
